full_judgment: 4. Mr. MA Rouf, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent, on the other hand, has urged that the Court of appeal below very rightly rejected the defendant's plea of auction purchase as the sale certificate or any document as to that purchase could not be produced in evidence by the defendants is support of the claim and as the defendants were pleading in the affirmative of the issue as to the existence of an auction sale the onus was upon them to prove the same and they having failed in substantiating their claim the court of appeal below committed an error of law or procedure in, coming to a finding of fact that the same could not be proved and in the absence of that auction purchase the Court had rightly declared plaintiffs saham to the extent of 1.44 acres of land in the suit property. Mr. Rouf has further urged vehemently that on top of the absence of any sale certificate there were no evidence as to the fact of delivery of possession of the property to the auction purchaser and title to the property never passed to auction purchaser and thereafter to the lessees as without any delivery of possession. I am afraid there is no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate in this regard because the law is otherwise. It had been consistently held in a number of cases that a sale certificate is not a title deed but it is. only an evidence of title and it is thus not incumbent upon the auction purchasers or his transferee to prove the right to the property only by proving into evidence the sale certificate as the said auction sale can be proved by any other evidence independent of the sale certificate (Ref: 24 CWN Page 111 and 1014 AIR 1950 Orissa page 213). A sale certificate thus is only an evidence of the auction sale like any other evidence with regard to it as title to the property .would pass to, the auction purchaser, under the provisions of Public Demand Recovery Act, after confirmation of the sale, independent of the sale certificate.
